ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there are two input terminals, respectively labeled A and B, which are connected to a rectangular logic function block. Inside the rectangle is marked “≥1”, indicating that when at least one input is 1, the block outputs 1. At the output terminal on the right side of the rectangle there is a small circle inversion mark, and after that it is connected to output terminal F. Reasoning: The internal “≥1” corresponds to OR logic, namely A + B; the small circle at the output terminal indicates inversion. Therefore the output of the entire circuit is inversion after OR, that is, the NOR relationship: F = overline(A + B).

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: inputs A and B feed a rectangular gate whose internal label is “≥1”; its output has a small inversion circle before the line labeled F. Interpret “≥1” as output 1 when at least one input is 1, i.e., OR: A+B. Apply the output bubble as NOT, giving F = overline(A+B).
